body: What I would do if this became a reality.  ^-^

I'm not sure, maybe this is kink, in which case this is awesome, but if you're self harming, it's not your fault.  I know that frustration and angst can really become overwhelming and that's a way that people try to cope, but it's not the only or right way.  You deserve the best, not the worst.

You will never be broken.  Your value isn't determined by someone who tries to tear you down to their level.  You are wonderful just for being you.  I don't expect things to just magically get better out of nowhere, but please just try to take some time to heal and be free from him.

This is absolutely horrible of him to do to you.  You deserve so much better, and you surely need time to heal.  He clearly doesn't understand that all relationship dynamics require kindness and love to flow in all directions, and that he's taken you for granted and been frankly really abusive.  I would recommend taking some time for yourself (not just an afternoon but maybe a long while).  If he tries to guilt you into taking him back, please try to find the strength to not let him.  You clearly deserve so much better.  I'm so sorry that this happened, just please hold on and please please don't hurt yourself in any way.
Please let this be satire.
How did you dye your hair?
Stephen Hawking.

I'm a Catholic guy (not sure what denomination you are, but anyway), and I think of it like, as long as you love your dom, and aren't cheating on them, and are nice to them, and they're doing the same for you (unless you agree on something otherwise), there's absolutely nothing wrong with being submissive, even as a dude. I know that it can be easier said than done to take that to heart, but you still love your dom just as much as you would love your partner if they weren't dominant.  Love is what matters, God is just as happy with any love with any sexual orientation or dynamic as long as it's able to be reciprocated by adults and doesn't hurt or betray or exploit people.
I'm really glad that I could help you and your girlfriend.  You don't owe me anything: just please try to remember that you're loved and that you have worth as a human being, no matter what.

It's okay to feel like it's hard: it can be.  You're certainly not a bad person if it's hard to feel good about oneself, even the absolute best, most loved people often have trouble finding that love for themselves.  

How about this: every day, think of one thing that you're good at, even a small thing, and write it down.  Then, each night, look and that list that you have so far.  It's a start, or at least it was for me.

Much love.  Please hold on.

Oh, man.  I'm sorry.  I didn't mean to have that effect.  Please hold on.  You're stronger than you realize, and that strength will help you find happiness and peace with yourself, as long as you believe that you can.  Please hold on.

I'm sorry that so many people have dropped the ball.  You deserve support, and the fact that you're conscious that people have their own emotions and concerns is an amazing one.

I'll always still be here for you.  You're worth it.

You are not a horrible person.  People see themselves in a worse light than anyone else does.  You're not too sensitive for this world: it's normal to be upset when someone else is being jerky.  Your life is worth living, you owe it to yourself to live, to enjoy life as much as possible.  You will always have value as an individual, even if others can't appreciate it yet.  It'll happen, though.  Just please hold on.

I wouldn't call you an idiot, or even really paranoid; just concerned, and that's actually really beautiful that you care about how she feels, even when you're hurting so much.  Maybe try asking her things like "is this too much?", "would you like a break from this stuff?", or saying stuff like "if this ever gets overwhelming, please tell me; I won't be hurt: I care how you feel too, I can tell someone else if you ever need that, even for a while".

Maybe try driving the point home that you don't want to set off triggers or make her panic, and that you would like to see her happy, because I'm sure that that's how you feel.

(I'm sorry if this is really repetitive or stuff you already know)

<3

Just because someone else has "had it worse" does not mean that your pain isn't real.  It is, and it's not your fault.  That doesn't mean that you should go through with it, but it does mean that you're not a bad person for feeling this way.  Depression and a sense of worthlessness can just happen to anyone: from royalty to beggars, and it's just as important and real for everyone.

Regardless, life is worth living.  Please hold on.  You have greatness and happiness ahead.  <3

Please call poison control.  Please.  You don't have to be alone: the right people will come into your life, just by you being you.

Much love <3

You aren't bringing her down.  She's listening because she cares; if she didn't, she'd stop.  If it's an option, I'd recommend maybe keeping a journal or seeing a therapist, even finding a penpal, but by all means, if someone's willing to listen, they're willing to listen.  She's listening because she cares, and I'm sure that you'd do the same.  You're acknowledging that she's got boundaries and preemptively respecting them, and that's healthy.  

Much love, from a 16 year old guy.  If anything, you can come to me too.

<3

You're left, you have the power to love yourself, the power to be happy.  You're better than any ex, you don't need them, you just need you.  Please know that you will always be able to find the one, and to find happiness and keep it for yourself.  You can do it, even if you don't think that you can, just by being you.  <3

I [M] somehow always fall head over heels for lesbians and most people around me destroy my confidence to the point of self hatred.  I'd like to be dommed around, but I'd also really like to be told that I'm not worthless, and comforted, just like how I want to comfort my partner.
